x-fc-resources.title: Recursos del SDK
x-fc-resources.description: Qué operación de la especificación es cada método de cada recurso. Son los mismos recursos y los mismos nombres que funnelchat-node (src/resources/*.ts en feat/inicial @ 88557ce), para que los dos SDKs se lean igual. El generador (`composer generate`) arma src/Resources/*.php con esto y con la especificación: los parámetros, la query, el cuerpo y la respuesta de cada método salen de la operación. Si una operación de esta lista ya no está en la especificación, la generación falla y dice cuál.

fields.traits: Traits escritos a mano que suma la clase.
fields.methods[].op: `MÉTODO /ruta`, tal como está en la especificación.
fields.methods[].paginate: Devuelve un Paginator (todas las páginas con foreach) en vez de la respuesta.
fields.methods[].doc: El comentario del método. Empieza con la operación entre comillas invertidas.
fields.methods[].query: `false` quita el parámetro `$query` (como en Node); `true` lo pone aunque la especificación no declare query. Si falta: está cuando la operación declara query o cuando pagina.
fields.methods[].bodyOptional: El cuerpo se puede omitir (como en Node). Si falta, el cuerpo es un argumento obligatorio cuando la operación lo tiene.
fields.methods[].bodyDefaults: Campos del cuerpo que, si no los pasas, se completan con un parámetro de ruta (y en el tipo quedan opcionales).

resources.doc: Contacts (conversations area): search, create, update, custom fields, notes and the 24-hour window.

methods.name: upsert
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/contacts/update-or-create`: creates the contact or updates the one with that phone.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/contacts/delete`: deletes the contacts of the body (`contactIds`, or a filter).

methods.name: attachCustomField
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/contacts/attach-custom-field`: sets a custom field on contacts.

methods.name: metaWindow
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/contacts/{contact}/meta-window`: whether the 24-hour window with the contact is open on a WhatsApp Cloud number (`is_open`). Outside it, only templates can be sent.

methods.name: listByDevice
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/devices/{device}/contacts`, paginated: the contacts of one number.

resources.doc: Conversations (conversations area): the inbox, its counters and the state of each conversation.

methods.name: update
methods.doc: `PUT /api/v1/contacts/{contact}/update`: changes the conversation with a contact (open, assigned…).

resources.doc:
Messages to one contact (conversations area): send text, files and buttons, read the history or one message by id, forward, react.

Sending with an API key needs the `conversations:send` permission and is subject to the WhatsApp rules: `422 window_closed`, `422 antiblock_*`, `422 recipient_*`, `422 device_unavailable`, `429 rate_limited` (with `retryAfter`) and `429 mac_lockout_24h`. A rejected send goes nowhere (see `Funnelchat\Exception\SendErrors`). Send operations are never retried automatically unless you pass `retrySend: true`.

methods.name: send
methods.doc:
`POST /api/v1/contacts/{contact}/message`: text, a file (`file` with a URL) or buttons and lists (`options`). Returns `['message' => …]`: the registered message, with its `id` and `status` `queued`. Queued is not sent: the next states arrive by `message.status_changed`, or read them with `get()`.

Send `phone` (or `whatsapp_id`) of the same contact: the API validates it. `contact_id` is optional: it defaults to the contact of the route. A file from a URL that does not show its format (signed, or without extension) needs `file_type`; a document like that, `file_name` with its extension. `client_reference` comes back in the message, the history and `message.status_changed`.

methods.name: sendDirect
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/message/send-message`: the same send with the contact in the body (`contact_id`, required). Returns `['message' => …]`, as `send()`. It is a send: same rules as `send()`.

methods.name: sendForm
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/contacts/{contact}/message/form`: sends a published WhatsApp form (`form_id` is the form's `family_id`) as a message with a button that opens it. Returns `['message' => …]` with `type` `whatsapp_form`; the answers arrive by `whatsapp_form.completed`. It is a send: same rules as `send()`.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/contacts/{contactId}/messages`, paginated by cursor: the history of a contact, with the `client_reference` of each send.

methods.name: get
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/contacts/{contact}/messages/{message}`: one message by the id a send or a webhook gave you (`message_id` of `message.status_changed`), with its current `status` and `error`. Any refusal is a `404`.

methods.name: sendContactCard
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/contacts/{contact}/message/contact-card`: sends up to 5 contact cards. Returns `['messages' => […]]`, one registered message per card, in order.

methods.name: forward
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/contacts/{contact}/messages/{message}/forward`: forwards a message to up to 5 contacts. Returns one item per target, in order: `status` `queued` or `blocked` (with `reason`) and its `message`.

resources.doc: WhatsApp message templates (conversations area): list, create, edit, send.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/templates`: creates a template and submits it to Meta.

methods.name: send
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/devices/{device}/templates/{template}/send-template`: sends an approved template (the way to write to a contact outside the 24-hour window). `phone` and `contact_id` are required; `template_variables.body` fills the body variables in order. Returns `['message' => …]`, the registered message (`type` `template`).

resources.doc:
WhatsApp Forms (conversations area): build them, version and publish them, choose their numbers, and read the answers. To send one to a contact, `messages->sendForm()`.

A form has versions: the `{id}` routes take a VERSION id, the `families/{familyId}` routes the form's id (`family_id`). Reading needs `conversations:read`, changing `conversations:write` and sending `conversations:send`. The answers also arrive by `whatsapp_form.completed`.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/forms`, paginated: one row per form, with its current version.

methods.name: templates
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/forms/templates`: the templates to start a form from (`blank` is an empty one).

methods.name: create
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/forms`: creates a draft from a template (`template_key`) for a number.

methods.name: retrieve
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/forms/{id}`: one version (`id` is the version id), with its lint issues, versions and numbers.

methods.name: update
methods.doc: `PUT /api/v1/forms/{id}`: saves a draft. A published version answers `409 PUBLISHED`; with `expected_updated_at`, someone else's change answers `409 STALE`.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: `DELETE /api/v1/forms/{id}`: deletes a draft (a published form is deprecated, not deleted).

methods.name: createVersion
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/forms/{id}/versions`: a new draft from this version, or the draft that already existed (`created: false`).

methods.name: sync
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/forms/{id}/sync`: validates the version in Meta (`502 META` when Meta rejects it).

methods.name: publish
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/forms/{id}/publish`: publishes the version (`422 LINT` with errors).

methods.name: numbers
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/forms/{id}/numbers`: the numbers of the form and their state.

methods.name: removeNumber
methods.doc: `DELETE /api/v1/forms/{id}/numbers/{deviceId}`: removes a number (not the primary one).

methods.name: definition
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/forms/families/{familyId}/definition`: the published definition of a form (`familyId`), or `data: null`.

methods.name: versions
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/forms/families/{familyId}/versions`, paginated: the versions of a form.

methods.name: listResponses
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/forms/families/{familyId}/responses`, paginated: the answers to a form, with `columns`.

methods.name: metrics
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/forms/families/{familyId}/metrics`: the funnel: sent, delivered, read, completed and the rates.

methods.name: listContacts
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/tags/{tag}/contacts`, paginated: the contacts with a tag.

resources.doc: Custom fields of contacts (conversations area). To set a value on a contact, see `contacts->attachCustomField()`.

WhatsApp groups (communities area): read groups, and act on them by API: create, manage participants and admins, name, description, photo, settings, invite link, send a message, and join requests.

Group actions are asynchronous: each one answers `202` with `action_id` and `status: queued`; follow it with `action()` or the `group_action.completed` / `group_action.failed` events. They are OFF by default: until communities turns them on, they answer `403 route_not_available` to any key. An official (Meta) number needs the `cloud-api-groups` beta (`422 provider_unsupported` without it).

methods.name: listByDevice
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/devices/{device}/groups`, paginated (`page`, `pageSize`): the groups of one number.

methods.name: metadata
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/groups/{groupUid}/metadata`: live metadata of a group by its WhatsApp uid, read through one number.

methods.name: listParticipants
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/groups/participants`, paginated: the participants of one group (`groupUid`).

methods.name: create
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/groups`: creates a group (`communities:operate`). On a QR number `participants` is required (up to 20); on an official one it is not allowed.

methods.name: action
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/groups/actions/{action}`: an action you requested, with its `status` (`queued`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`), `result` and `reason`.

methods.name: addParticipants
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/groups/{group}/participants`: adds participants (an official number invites them).

methods.name: updateDescription
methods.doc: `PUT /api/v1/groups/{group}/description`: changes the description (`null` or empty clears it on a QR number).

methods.name: updatePhoto
methods.doc: `PUT /api/v1/groups/{group}/photo`: changes the photo from a public `https` URL to a `.jpg`, `.jpeg` or `.png` (QR numbers only).

methods.name: updateSettings
methods.doc: `PUT /api/v1/groups/{group}/settings`: whether members can send messages (QR numbers only).

methods.name: renewInviteLink
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/groups/{group}/invite-link/renew`: revokes the invite link and creates a new one.

methods.name: inviteLink
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/groups/{group}/invite-link/live`: the current invite link, read live through `device_id` (cached 30 seconds).

methods.name: sendMessage
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/groups/{group}/messages`: sends text or a file (`media_url`) to a group (`communities:send`). A send: never retried automatically.

methods.name: listJoinRequests
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/groups/{group}/join-requests`: the pending join requests (up to 100), read live. Official numbers and groups only.

methods.name: approveJoinRequests
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/groups/{group}/join-requests/approve`: approves join requests by phone. Official numbers only, behind an option communities keeps off.

methods.name: rejectJoinRequests
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/groups/{group}/join-requests/reject`: rejects join requests by phone. Official numbers only, behind an option communities keeps off.

resources.doc: WhatsApp numbers of the account (accounts area). The `id` of a number is the `device_id` used to send.

methods.name: me
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/devices/{device}/me`: the WhatsApp profile of the number.

resources.doc:
Webhook subscriptions (accounts area) and the verification of deliveries.

The subscription routes need `webhooks:read` / `webhooks:write`, and a key only sees and manages subscriptions whose events are of areas it can read (`{area}:read`). The catalog (`events()`) needs `accounts:read`. PENDING OF THE SPEC: the subscription routes come from accounts v1.4.24, not from the snapshot; their types are in spec/pending.json until a snapshot brings them.

methods.name: events
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/webhooks/events`: the event types you can subscribe to, each with `status`.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/webhooks`, paginated: the subscriptions of the account (at most 50), not only yours, except those with events of an area your key cannot read.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/webhooks`: the response brings `secret` once. Store it, and store the `id`.

methods.name: rotateSecret
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/rotate-secret`: the new secret comes once; the old one stops working. Not open to API keys in accounts v1.4.24: it answers `403 route_not_available` (rotate it in the panel).

methods.name: listDeliveries
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries`, paginated: one row per attempt, newest first.
